finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF. The /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get and returns the response body to the caller. There is no scheme, host or IP validation. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) and localhost, and read the responses.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the response body copied to the client at main.go:22

trace.note: Route /fetch registered with no auth middleware
target read from the query string
http.Get(target) issues the request; redirects are followed by default
Full response body is returned to the attacker (non-blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. No allowlist, scheme check, IP or private-range filtering, or auth. The /safe handler's allowlist is not applied to /fetch.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 pass the query param `target` directly to http.Get with no validation, main.go:22 returns the body, and main.go:41 registers /fetch bare (no auth); the allowlist at main.go:27 applies only to /safe.
